title: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
shortTitle: 2025 AHA adult ALS: IV first; avoid unproven arrest adjuncts
summary: The 2025 adult ALS guideline recommends attempting IV access first during adult cardiac arrest; IO is reasonable when IV access fails or is infeasible. Head-up CPR is not recommended outside clinical trials. POCUS for reversible causes or prognostication remains insufficiently established.
whyItMatters: Keep local arrest protocols centered on high-quality CPR, early indicated defibrillation and established therapies. Avoid letting an ultrasound examination interrupt compressions or determine prognosis in isolation.
limitations: Recommendation strength differs substantially across interventions; limited evidence for adjuncts should not be confused with proven harm. This article covers adult ALS, not the entire pediatric, special-circumstances or post-arrest guideline set.
population: Adults with cardiac arrest, peri-arrest arrhythmias and life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies.
findings: IV-first access: Class 1, Level A; IO after unsuccessful/infeasible IV: Class 2a, Level A.
Head-up CPR outside trials: Class 3, No Benefit, Level C-LD.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. Official AHA full-text HTML at https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-advanced-life-support reviewed, including access/adjunct recommendation tables. Journal endpoint returned 403; no access controls bypassed. First electronic publication October 22, 2025 confirmed by PubMed and AHA release; print labeling October 21 was not used.
guidelineStrength: Individual COR/LOE assignments apply; POCUS for reversible causes and prognostication is Class 2b, Level C-LD.
